chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, he raised it (to the Imam), saying:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed by the butchers and forbade them from selling seven things from the sheep: he forbade them from selling blood, glands, ears of the heart, the liver, the spleen, the testicles, and the penis. Some of the butchers said to him, 'O Commander of the Faithful, the liver and the spleen are the same.' He said to him, 'You lied, O Luk'aa. Bring me two jars of water, and I will inform you of the difference between them.' So a liver and a spleen were brought, along with two jars of water. He said, 'Split the liver from its middle and the spleen from its middle.' Then he ordered that they all be poured with water. The liver turned white and nothing was lost from it, but the spleen did not turn white, and all that was inside it came out and became entirely blood, and skin and veins remained. He said to him, 'This is the difference between them. This is meat, and this is blood.'
ai.seo_question: What are the seven prohibited parts of the sheep in Shia jurisprudence and how did Imam Ali distinguish between liver and spleen?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) prohibits the sale of seven specific sheep parts, using a practical demonstration to distinguish between the liver (labeled as meat) and the spleen (labeled as blood) based on their physical reaction to water. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on empirical observation in deriving fiqh rulings regarding food purity and commerce. The distinction underscores the nuanced classification of animal parts in Islamic dietary law, moving beyond simple anatomical similarity to functional and textual categorization.
